complete_closure_policy.authority_seat_scope: one key ID and one identity/organization pair may span gaps only under one unchanged authority class
complete_closure_policy.validation_entrypoint_identity: complete_closure module, acceptance alias, package API and CLI share one immutable aggregate-bounded snapshot wrapper
complete_closure_policy.runtime_authority: supported operational entrypoints use current trusted system time and root-owned non-group/world-writable /usr/bin/openssl by absolute path under a minimal deterministic environment; caller time, executable, PATH, OpenSSL configuration, module path and dynamic-loader overrides are rejected or discarded
complete_closure_policy.lexical_scope_custody: validation and high-level signing commands retain canonical lexical names; roots, parents, files and signing keys are opened no-follow; shared ancestor directory identities are pinned across each complete transaction; bundle input, detached signature and immutable successor must remain in one custody generation; visible names must retain the opened objects
complete_closure_policy.contract_semantic_binding: issuer, evidence-set and reviewer digests bind the canonical SHA-256 of the complete current contract object in addition to its revision label
complete_closure_policy.committed_accepted_envelope_discovery: recursive content identity under evidence/external through filesystem-anchor and child directory descriptors, with no-follow traversal and stable lexical/opened/post-read object identity

authority_owned.closure_rule: Every authority class named for a gap signs exactly its versioned class-scoped claims. Seats are distinct inside each gap and cannot cross authority classes. Validation and signing share canonical contract binding, final-review context, trusted runtime, lexical object identity and one transaction-wide custody generation. Real external evidence and independent acceptance remain required.

claim_ceiling: G10 closes repository-controlled authority quorum, role aliasing, claim and contract binding, review integrity, validation and signing custody, trusted cryptographic execution, and committed-package admission only; it does not create administrative, physical, provider, vendor, independent-assurance, production-signing, pilot, store, deployment, or release facts.
